summary: How much loot is on the floor, how much of it a player is shown, the 2017-06-29 laminated armour rules and the airdrop channel. D270/D271/D272 (2026-09-03) raised the floor to the ruled 0.27 density, made Gear01's gate the clothing gate and cut the gun cluster to one box; that retired three of the six THIRD_PARTY_SHAPED rows this file used to carry. D286 (2026-09-03 evening) then reversed D272, putting the gun cluster back to TWO boxes after the owner played the one-box world. The two that remain - FirstAidKit01 0.30 and Ammo01 0.60 - are the owner's own gates that already sat ABOVE the ruled density, so the ruling left them where he put them; docs/39 s1.1 and docs/65 s2.2 trace their shape to a reference server's Z2 ground tables and D68 adopted them under D53, and they are recorded THIRD_PARTY_SHAPED here rather than being silent about it (S8 s5.1, docs/96 s5).

rows.source: docs/39 s4.2 / D31 - Cranberry's own solve, ruled the floor density by the owner on 2026-09-03
rows.note: D270 (2026-09-03), the owner's floor-density ruling: spawn chance 0.27 replacing the weighted 0.1223. The value itself is docs/39 s4.2's own solve (D31) - Cranberry's measurement of the client's marker spacing, 12.45 markers to a 4 m room over 4,000 samples, against the owner's retail-footage census of 0-6 loose items per room, mean about 3. AUDIT-loot.md G1 measured the shortfall his gates produced: 1.50 items in a 4 m room against that counted mean of 3. Was 0.1267 (his 18 % over a 405-weight pool with a 120 "empty" row, D68, THIRD_PARTY_SHAPED); the ruling raises it to the ruled density and retires the grade with it. Mirrors SPAWN_CHANCES in tools/data/gen-loot-tables.py, which is what the runtime actually reads through z2-loot-tables.json.

rows.source: AUDIT-loot.md G3 - Gear01's own marker share, 96,722 of 168,322 = 57.5 %
rows.note: D271 (2026-09-03), THE CLOTHING GATE, the owner's ruling: "raise the clothing gate so shirts/boots are common on floors" against his own note "floors covered in folded shirts and work boots", with the number to come from the audit's Gear01 marker share. A family gated at the flat ruled density produces its own share of the MARKERS as its share of the FLOOR, so ruling Gear01 to 0.27 is exactly the statement "Gear01 gets the 57.5 % of the floor the client's own marker field gives it". Was 0.0850 - the LOWEST of the five gates on the family that owns 57.5 % of the markers, which is why clothing was 6.8 % of the floor. Measured at seed 1: Gear01 40.1 % -> 57.2 % of items, clothing 6.9 % -> 12.3 % of ground objects (2,060 -> 6,145 garments map-wide).

rows.source: the owner, 2026-09-03 evening, reversing D272: "there's only one ammo box now next to guns? It should be two"
rows.note: D286 REVERSES D272 back to TWO boxes per gun: the owner played the one-box world and ruled it back to two. D272 had cut the pair to one on the strength of AUDIT-loot.md G2, which measured the two-box world: 34.7 % of every ground object was an ammunition box, boxes outnumbered weapons 1.77:1, the median nearest-neighbour distance on the whole floor was exactly 0.50 m (the cluster offset) and the dominant non-singleton cluster was size 3 - a gun and its two boxes. That is the world the owner has chosen back. The client corroborates PAIRING only for the 72 Ammo01 markers (36 pairs 0.65-0.68 m apart) and those are marker rolls, untouched by either ruling. Measured at seed 1 with D270's gates: two boxes put ammunition at ~34.8 % of ground objects (one box was 20.2 %). The number ships inside z2-loot-tables.json's clusters block so it is retunable without a rebuild; LootRosterRulingsTests pins the two copies equal.

rows.source: retail, dated 2017-06-29, High confidence: C:/Aug2017/out/stage1-assessment/web-research-aug2017-kotk.md:136 "Laminated (Tactical) Armor - cannot be crafted; from June 29 2017: world spawn chance cut 10 % -> 5 %, 250 m anti-cluster radius, max 3 per map square, bulk 500 -> 1000, guaranteed in every airdrop; absorbs 2 bullets."
rows.note: AUDIT-loot.md G5: Cranberry had a flat weight of 18/608 inside Gear01 and no spacing rule at all. Expressed here as retail expressed it - an explicit world chance applied AFTER the marker has already rolled the vest, drawn from the marker's own third sub-stream so changing it never re-shuffles the rest of the map. Measured at seed 1 under D270/D271: 700 vests roll, 35 pass this chance, 11 are then refused by the 250 m radius, 0 by the per-square cap - 24 vests on the whole map.

rows.source: the same 2017-06-29 sentence: "250 m anti-cluster radius"
rows.note: Enforced in Z2LootLayout's deterministic layout pass, in ascending ZONE instance-id order so the same seed keeps the same 24 vests on any machine. It is the rule that actually binds at the ruled chance (11 refusals at seed 1).

rows.source: the same 2017-06-29 sentence: "max 3 per map square"
rows.note: A ceiling guard rather than the binding rule: at the ruled 5 % the 250 m radius has already spaced the vests below it and this suppresses none at seed 1. LootArmourTests proves it binds by driving the chance to 1.0.

rows.source: Cranberry's own: the Z2 terrain's +-4,096 m extent (docs/29 s2.1) in an 8 x 8 grid
rows.note: UNPROVEN SIZE. Retail's sentence says "per map square" and this build ships no map-grid definition of any kind - searched Models.txt, the datasheets and out/world_aug. The client's own terrain squares are the 128 m .cnk chunks (docs/29 s2), which are far smaller than the 250 m radius and would make the cap meaningless, so this rules the map square as the map itself in an 8 x 8 grid: 64 squares, a global ceiling of 192 vests. If a real map-grid size is ever read out of the client, this row is the one line to change.

docs/112 s2 - D69's own rule (the measured peak plus about a sixth of headroom) re-applied after each density change: peak working set 497 at one box gave 576, and D286's second box per gun raised the peak to 612, so 704 carries ~15 %
rows.note: 128 before D69, 384 from D69, 576 from D281, 704 after D286. D69 sized 384 against a measured peak of 341 on a 19,475-item floor; D270 doubled the floor to 39,346 and the same sweep measured 497, so D281 raised it to 576; D286 (reversing D272 to two boxes per gun) added ~10,000 more ground entities and the same sweep now measures a peak of 612, so 576 TRUNCATED the working set again. Measured with the cap lifted to 100,000 the two-box peak is 612 and does not grow further, which is what makes 704 a guard rail again rather than a budget. Doorway coverage is unchanged by the cap at any value (100 % median / 80 % worst), so this fixes the truncation and not the coverage - see docs/112 s7.
